summary: The cluster tests twelve Conway UTXO-level rules (inputs present, inputs non-empty, FeesOk/collateral, ref-input disjointness, metadata, output min-ADA and value size, validity interval, collateral count, tx size, treasury value, value conservation) in 12 suites, 3.3k lines, about 1.6 s per run; the 0.45 s and 0.19 s first tests of FeesOk and AllInputs are JVM warm-up of Arbitrary, so there is no ci-time finding (C7). Statement coverage is high but hides weak tests: FeesOk failure tests fail for two reasons each, so the fee >= minFee, non-ADA, sufficiency and has-collateral checks can be deleted without a failing test (C19-1, C19-2); most other failure tests assert only isLeft (C19-6); one disjointness test runs at PV11 where the rule is off (C19-5); boundaries of min-ADA, value size and the validity lower bound are untested (C19-7); the Plutus-script part of the metadata check and the BadInputs path of value conservation never run (C19-8, C19-15). Fixtures are mostly random (randomTransactionWithIsValidField, unseeded Arbitrary samples), which blocks exact assertions and causes a real 0.1 % flake in two ValueNotConserved tests (C19-14); TreasuryValueMismatchValidatorTest and the overflow half of ValueNotConservedUTxOValidatorTest are the models. The cluster has no property test and uses generators only for fixtures (C8); the one generator fact that matters is the empty-AssetName collision. Simplification (FeesOk builders, Metadata and validity tables, ValueNotConserved table + property) removes about 1.9k lines. No main-bug: FeesOk check 4 was compared with Babbage validateCollateralContainsNonADA and InputsAndReferenceInputsDisjoint with Babbage disjointRefInputs (cardano-ledger-conway-1.22.1.0); both match. Related: C02-16/C02-17/C02-18 (ledger.rules.scripts) propose the same fixture cleanup and shared builders for ValidatorRulesTestKit.

behaviors.name: spend, collateral and reference inputs that are all in the UTxO pass (incl. all empty)
a missing input of any kind fails; each kind is reported in its own set
a tx with no spend inputs fails
fee >= minFee (both the no-redeemer path and the redeemer path)
no redeemers: collateral checks are skipped
collateral at a non-VKey address fails
non-ADA in collateral must all go to the collateral return
collateral ADA balance >= fee * collateralPercentage / 100
totalCollateral, when present, equals the collateral ADA balance
at least one collateral input
a collateral input missing from the UTxO, or a minFee error, gives BadCollateralInputs / BadReferenceInputs
ref-script fee term accepted at PV11 for a tx that spends and references one UTxO
inputs and reference inputs overlap: rejected only at PV 9 and 10
hash/data presence: none ok, hash-only and data-only fail
the aux data hash must equal blake2b_256 of the raw aux data bytes
bytes and text (UTF-8 bytes) at most 64, checked inside lists and map keys/values
no content check at PV <= 2 (Shelley)
Plutus V1/V2/V3 scripts in the aux data must be well formed
outputs and collateral return need coin >= minAda and no negative assets
serialized Value of outputs and collateral return at most maxValueSize
slot in [invalidBefore, invalidHereafter), each bound optional
collateral inputs at most maxCollateralInputs
size without the isValid flag at most maxTxSize, exact boundary
currentTreasuryValue must equal env treasury, only when isValid
inputs, outputs and fee balance; output > input fails
mint counts as consumed, burn as produced
withdrawals consumed, donation produced
pool deposits: new pool pays once, re-registration pays none; declared cert deposits
sums are exact past Long.MaxValue; error clamps to Long
a spend input missing from the UTxO gives BadInputsUTxOException
public Value-returning consumed(...)

findings.claim: Five of the six FeesOk failure tests fail for two reasons and assert only isLeft, so they cannot detect the loss of the check they name. 'fee too low' (170-270) also has totalCollateral 60 ADA against a net 40 ADA (30+30-20), so check 6 fails too. 'return has more tokens' (367-476) and 'return has less tokens' (479-591) have the same 60-vs-40 ADA totalCollateral mismatch. 'collateral insufficient' (593-693) has inputs 60 ADA, return 60 ADA, so the net is 0 against totalCollateral 60 ADA (check 6 fails as well). 'no collateral input' (797-857) has a balance of 0, which fails check 5 for fee 10 ADA at the mainnet collateralPercentage of 150. Only 'VKey address' (272-365) and 'totalCollateral mismatch' (695-795) isolate their check. Mutations that the suite does not catch: delete `!isTransactionFeeGreaterOrEqualThanMinRequiredFee ||`, `remainingAssets.nonEmpty ||`, `!isCollateralSufficient ||` or `!hasCollateralInputs` from FeesOkValidator.scala:105-110. With C19-2 (the fee-too-low branch at 61-75 is uncovered), no test in this suite fails when 'fee >= minFee' breaks.
findings.action: Make each failure case one change from the passing baseline (10-117), and assert the exact FeesOkException fields that name the reason. Fee too low: totalCollateral = 40 ADA, fee = 1; assert error.minRequiredFee > error.transactionFee. Tokens: totalCollateral = 40 ADA; assert error.remainingAssets is the unreturned (or negative) MultiAsset. Insufficient: drop totalCollateral, return 59 ADA so the net is 1 ADA; assert actualTotalSumOfCollateralCoins == 1 ADA. No collateral: check 5 always fails here, so either set collateralPercentage = 0 in the context and assert Left, or assert hasCollateralInputs == false on the exception. Use the field-match style of 859-901.
findings.coverageRisk: none: assertions become stricter; the same scenarios stay

findings.claim: The baseline marks three FeesOkValidator paths unexecuted in the whole jvm/test: a collateral input missing from the UTxO (BadCollateralInputsUTxOException, line 37), computeMinFee returning Left (line 51: a reference input or spend input missing from the UTxO gives BadReferenceInputsUTxOException / BadInputsUTxOException), and the no-redeemer branch with fee < minFee (64-75). The collateral-percentage boundary is also untested: every case is either well above or well below fee * 150 / 100.
findings.action: Add to FeesOkValidatorTest: (1) collateral input absent from State.utxos -> Left(BadCollateralInputsUTxOException(tx.id)); (2) a reference input absent from utxos -> Left(BadReferenceInputsUTxOException); (3) no redeemers, fee = 0 -> Left(FeesOkException) with areTotalExUnitsZero = true; (4) redeemers present, collateral ADA balance exactly ceil(fee * 150 / 100) -> Right, and one lovelace less -> Left (as in CollateralSufficient: balance * 100 >= fee * pct).

findings.claim: Eight FeesOk tests repeat about 90 lines each: randomTransactionWithIsValidField followed by 13 body-field resets and 9 witness-set resets back to empty, two generateKeyPair calls whose private keys are unused (17-18 and five more pairs), a key-hash address built by copying an Arbitrary ShelleyAddress, a `given Arbitrary[Data]` that nothing uses (11-13, repeated in 8 tests), and a random redeemer tag/index/ExUnits that the validator ignores. The last test (859-901) shows the short form: Transaction(TransactionBody(...), witnessSet with one fixed Redeemer).
findings.action: Add a local builder collateralTx(fee, collateral: Map[TransactionInput, Value], collateralReturn: Option[Value], totalCollateral: Option[Coin], redeemers = true): (State, Transaction) using Transaction(TransactionBody(...)) and a fixed Redeemer(RedeemerTag.Spend, 0, Data.unit, ExUnits(1000, 1000)), with fixed inputs and one key address (see C19-16). Rewrite tests 10-857 on it and delete the unused givens and key pairs. Do it together with C19-1, which changes the same tests.
findings.coverageRisk: none: same scenarios, same assertions; random fields the validator ignores are removed

findings.claim: 'rule failure' (31-62) builds the same full-overlap tx at PV10 and asserts Left; 'allows overlap since PV11' (64-82) builds it at the default PV11 and asserts Right. The table test (84-107) runs the same tx at PV 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 with the same isRight assertion, so its rows 10 and 11 are these two tests.
findings.action: Delete 31-82. Keep the table at 84-107 and give its PV 9/10 rows the exact error (see C19-5).
findings.coverageRisk: none: the table rows PV10 -> rejected and PV11 -> accepted assert the same outcomes on the same kind of tx
findings.verification: All three tests are in the same shared/ file and call the same entry point, InputsAndReferenceInputsDisjointValidator.validate. 'rule failure' (InputsAndReferenceInputsDisjointValidatorTest.scala:31-62) runs at PV(10,0) and asserts isLeft (:55). Its other two asserts (:56-61) only check how the test built the tx (inputs non-empty, inputs == refInputs). They check nothing in the validator. 'allows overlap since PV11' (:64-82) uses the default Context and asserts isRight (:81). The table (:84-107) builds the same tx (inputs == refInputs, 1-4 random inputs). It sets PV(10,0) -> false and PV(11,0) -> true explicitly (:98-106) and asserts isRight == accepted. The validator reads only protocolVersion.major (InputsAndReferenceInputsDisjointValidator.scala:38-40). So the explicit PV11 row is at least as strong as the default-context test. Deleting :31-82 loses no validator assertion.

findings.claim: 'InputsAndReferenceInputsDisjointValidator rule success' (7-29) runs with Context(), whose default params are PV11, where the validator returns success at line 15-16 before it looks at the inputs. The test cannot fail for any change to the disjointness check. The asserts at InputsAndRef 26-28, 56-61 and EmptyInputs 25, 44 check the fixture the test just built, not the validator, so no main-code mutation breaks them. No test has a partial overlap, and no test checks that the error reports exactly the intersection.
findings.action: Pin the success test to PV10 and give it disjoint non-empty inputs and reference inputs. Add a PV10 partial-overlap case: inputs {a, b}, reference inputs {b, c} -> Left(NonDisjointInputsAndReferenceInputsException(tx.id, Set(b))). Delete the fixture asserts at InputsAndRef 26-28, 56-61 and EmptyInputs 25, 44.
findings.coverageRisk: none: removes assertions that cannot fail and adds cases

findings.claim: Every failure test in AllInputs, EmptyInputs, TooManyCollateral, OutputsHaveNotEnoughCoins and OutputsHaveTooBigValueStorageSize asserts only isLeft. Mutations no test catches: swap the missingInputs and missingCollateralInputs arguments of BadAllInputsUTxOException (AllInputsMustBeInUtxoValidator.scala:24-26); report an empty invalidOutputs or drop invalidCollateralReturnOutput in OutputsHaveNotEnoughCoinsException (22-28); report the wrong size or maxValueSize in OutputsHaveTooBigValueStorageSizeException; swap actual and max in TooManyCollateralInputsException. TreasuryValueMismatchValidatorTest:40-51 already asserts the exact Left.
findings.action: Replace each `assert(result.isLeft)` with `assert(result == Left(<Exception>(tx.id, ...)))` that names the expected sets, outputs, sizes and limits, as TreasuryValueMismatchValidatorTest:40-51 does. Requires fixed fixtures (C19-11) so the expected values are known.

findings.claim: The boundaries of three rules are untested. OutputsHaveNotEnoughCoins uses coin 1 lovelace or 1000 ADA, so the mutation `coin < minAda` -> `coin <= minAda` (line 41) survives. OutputsHaveTooBigValueStorageSize uses a small random value or a 10x100-asset value, so `>` -> `>=` (line 43) survives. OutsideValidityInterval with both bounds tests slots 499, 700 and 1000, so `slot >= invalidBefore` -> `slot > invalidBefore` in the both-bounds branch (line 35) survives. AllInputs never mixes kinds: no test has spend inputs present and a collateral input missing, so a validator that checks only the first non-empty set would pass.
findings.action: Add boundary rows. Min ADA: compute minAda = MinCoinSizedTransactionOutput.computeMinAda for the output, set coin = minAda, recompute and check it is stable (the coin's CBOR width changes the size; pick a value in one width class), then assert minAda -> Right and minAda - 1 -> Left. Value size: set maxValueSize = Cbor.encode(value).length -> Right and length - 1 -> Left, as TransactionWithoutIsValidTest:98-115 does for maxTxSize; do not try to build an exact 5000-byte value. Validity: (Some(500), Some(1000)) at slot 500 -> Right and 999 -> Right. AllInputs: spend input present, collateral and reference input missing -> Left with exactly those two sets.

findings.claim: The Plutus-script half of the aux-data check (isValidAuxiliaryPlutusScripts, lines 100-106) is unexecuted in the baseline of all modules: no test puts a script in AuxiliaryData.MetadataWithScripts or AlonzoFormat. The text-size test (186-214) uses 65 ASCII chars, so the mutation `str.getBytes(UTF_8).length` -> `str.length` (line 87) survives; Metadatum.Text has no constructor check. The PV gate (line 56) is tested only at PV 2 (skip) and the default PV 11 (check), so `<= shelleyPV` -> `< 11` survives.
findings.action: Add: (1) AlonzoFormat aux data with a malformed PlutusV1, V2 and V3 script (e.g. bytes that do not decode as a UPLC program) and a matching hash -> Left(InvalidAuxiliaryDataException); a well-formed script -> Right. (2) Metadatum.Text of 33 two-byte chars ("é" * 33 = 66 UTF-8 bytes, 33 chars) -> Left, and 32 of them (64 bytes) -> Right. (3) PV 3 with oversized metadata -> Left.

findings.claim: Eleven Metadata tests rebuild the same tx (empty inputs, empty outputs, fee 0, aux hash) and compute the blake2b_256 hash of KeepRaw(auxData).raw by hand (8 copies). The five invalid-metadatum tests (156-317) differ only in the Metadatum and are one table. Each failure test asserts isLeft and then left.exists(isInstanceOf), so the first assert is redundant.
findings.action: Add local helpers hashOf(aux) and txWith(aux: Option[AuxiliaryData], hash: Option[AuxiliaryDataHash]). Turn 156-317 into a table of (name, Metadatum) rows, each asserting Left(InvalidAuxiliaryDataException(tx.id, aux)). Replace isLeft + isInstanceOf with one exact-Left or pattern-match assert.
findings.coverageRisk: none: same cases and stronger assertions

findings.claim: The eight OutsideValidityInterval tests are copies of one 28-line body that differ in (invalidBefore, invalidHereafter, slot, expected). Each builds the tx from randomTransactionWithIsValidField and asserts only isRight/isLeft.
findings.action: Replace with one table of 8 rows (plus the C19-7 rows) over a tx built as Transaction(TransactionBody(inputs = empty, outputs = empty, fee = 0, validityStartSlot, ttl)). Failure rows assert Left(OutsideValidityIntervalException(tx.id, interval, slot)).

findings.claim: Seven suites build fixtures from randomTransactionWithIsValidField (an Arbitrary[Transaction] with random mint, certificates, withdrawals and witnesses) and then override the one or two fields under test; TooManyCollateral even draws two random txs per test and mixes them (21-23, 43-45). TransactionSizeValidatorTest:14-53 spends 40 lines resetting a random tx back to almost empty. OutputsHaveNotEnoughCoins copies an Arbitrary ShelleyAddress and replaces its payment part six times (12-21 and five more) to get a key address. AllInputs repeats one 18-line body seven times for {inputs, collateral, reference} x {present, missing}. The random fixtures also make exact-Left assertions (C19-6) impossible to write.
findings.action: Build each tx as Transaction(TransactionBody(inputs, outputs, fee, <field under test>)) as TreasuryValueMismatchValidatorTest:19-27 does, with fixed TransactionInput values (TransactionInput(TransactionHash.fromHex("0" * 64), i)) and a fixed key address (C19-16). Turn AllInputs into a table over the three input kinds. When ValidatorRulesTestKit gets the shared builders proposed in C02-18, use them; drop randomTransactionWithIsValidField if no caller remains (it has 13 users).
findings.coverageRisk: low: the random parts of the tx never reached these validators; a random mint or certificate cannot change their result

findings.claim: Both TransactionSizeValidator tests are weaker forms of TransactionWithoutIsValidTest:98-115, which sets maxTxSize to the exact 3-element size, asserts Right for both encodings and Left at size - 1. The local tests check a 1-input tx (Right) and a 1000-input tx (Left) at the mainnet limit, far from the boundary.
findings.action: Delete TransactionSizeValidatorTest.scala, or move the 98-115 boundary test into it and delete the two random tests. The covering test is in package scalus.cardano.ledger (another cluster); P3 must pick one home and not delete both.
findings.coverageRisk: low: the exact-boundary test covers both outcomes; it lives in another cluster, so a later edit there could drop it
findings.verification: Both files are in scalus-cardano-ledger/shared/src/test and call TransactionSizeValidator.validate. The validator compares toCborForFeeCalculation.length with params.maxTxSize (TransactionSizeValidator.scala:11-14). TransactionWithoutIsValidTest.scala:99-115 sets maxTxSize to the exact size and asserts isRight for the 3-element and 4-element encodings. It sets size-1 and asserts isLeft. This covers both branches at the boundary. The local tests are weaker: a 1-input tx -> isRight (TransactionSizeValidatorTest.scala:55) and a 1000-input tx -> isLeft (:76), both at the default limit. One minor difference: the random tx can have isValid=false, but neither local test checks the size value, so no assertion is lost. Caveat (already in the action): the covering test is in another cluster/package. P3 must keep it, or move it into TransactionSizeValidatorTest, before it deletes the file.

findings.claim: The first 19 tests (24-736, about 710 lines) are instances of one law: a tx whose consumed side (inputs + mint>0 + withdrawals) equals its produced side (outputs + fee + burn + donation) passes, and any other tx fails with ValueNotConservedUTxOException. Each test hand-builds the tx; 18 assert isRight and one (64-87) asserts only isLeft. The suite already has the right builder at 807-828 (balanceTx), used only by the overflow tests.
findings.action: Extend balanceTx with withdrawals and donation. Replace 24-736 with (a) a table of the named scenarios (one row each, about 3 lines) and (b) one forAll: generate 1-3 input Values, a mint (positive and negative), 0-2 withdrawals, an optional donation and a fee; compute the balancing output with plain sums over those components (not TxBalance, to avoid a circular oracle); assert Right; then add a non-zero delta of lovelace or of one token to an output and assert Left(ValueNotConservedUTxOException(tx.id, consumed, produced)) with the hand-computed sides. Keep the deposit tests (739-795) and the overflow tests (797-938) as they are. Land C19-14 first.
findings.coverageRisk: low: every named scenario stays as a table row; the property adds random combinations. The examples check only isRight, so no assertion is lost
findings.verification: There are 19 tests at ValueNotConservedUTxOValidatorTest.scala:24-736. 18 assert only isRight. One asserts only isLeft (:87). The law matches the main code. consumedExact = inputs + withdrawals + refunds + mint.onlyPositive (TxBalance.scala:39-63). producedExact = outputs + fee + deposits + proposalDeposits + burned + donation (:91-106). The validator compares these exactly (ValueNotConservedUTxOValidator.scala:26). ExactValue drops zero entries (ExactValue.scala:99), so a plain-sum oracle cannot fail on zero-quantity tokens. With no certificates or proposals, refunds and deposits are 0. Withdrawals are summed without a state check (TxBalance.scala:133-138). So no counterexample exists for the generated shape. Some examples have shapes the generator cannot produce: empty tx (:24), no outputs (:240), Some(Coin.zero) withdrawal/donation (:536, :595), a 2-policy mint (:297). The action keeps each of these as a table row, so no coverage is lost. Generator constraints P3 must apply: burns must not exceed the input holdings, and the coin balance must stay >= 0 after fee and donation. Otherwise the balancing output gets a negative amount. Use a positive delta (or a delta to the fee) for the Left case. Inputs/withdrawals are keyed by random createInput/reward accounts, and duplicates collapse in the Map (:812-814), so build the oracle from the deduplicated keys. Use fixed distinct asset names in the 'mint and burn same asset' row (:418-465). With random names it is a known flake: the two names can collide.

findings.claim: This fixes a flaky test. 'mint and burn same asset' (418-466) and 'complex transaction ...' (625-677) draw two unseeded random AssetNames. Arbitrary[AssetName] picks the length with Gen.choose(0, 32), so both names are empty with probability (1/33)^2, about 0.09 % per test per run (plus rarer 1-byte collisions). Then Map(assetName1 -> -100, assetName2 -> 50) collapses to one entry, the tx no longer balances, and the test fails. The suite also draws every input, address and policy id at random (14-17) with no seed.
findings.action: Use fixed values: AssetName.fromString("A") / ("B"), a fixed PolicyId, TransactionInput(TransactionHash.fromHex("0" * 64), i) and Party.Alice.address. Delete createInput/createAddress/createPolicyId/createAssetName.
findings.coverageRisk: none: the same balances; removes a nondeterministic failure

findings.claim: ValueNotConservedUTxOValidator returns BadInputsUTxOException when a spend input is not in the UTxO (TxBalance.consumedInputs, line 119, propagated at 41), but the baseline marks line 41 unexecuted: no test reaches it. The public TxBalance.consumed (24-30, which returns a Value and throws on overflow) is also unexecuted.
findings.action: Add to ValueNotConservedUTxOValidatorTest: a tx whose input is absent from State.utxos -> Left(BadInputsUTxOException(tx.id)). Add one test of TxBalance.consumed: it returns the consumed Value for a small tx, and throws ArithmeticException for the 4 x 2^62-token input of 867-877, as 849 does for produced.

findings.claim: FeesOkValidatorTest makes key-hash collateral addresses with generateKeyPair() + platform.blake2b_224(publicKey) + a copied Arbitrary ShelleyAddress (16 sites, 8 unused private keys). OutputsHaveNotEnoughCoins does the same with a random AddrKeyHash (6 sites). The shared scalus.testing.kit.Party gives deterministic key addresses: Party.Alice.address(Network.Testnet). ValueNotConservedUTxOValidatorTest:917-918 already uses it.
findings.action: Replace these sites with Party.Alice.address(Network.Testnet) / Party.Bob.address(...). For the script-address case in FeesOk (272-365) use Address(Network.Testnet, Credential.ScriptHash(<fixed hash>)). With C02-17 this can remove generateKeyPair from ValidatorRulesTestKit.
findings.coverageRisk: none: the validators only check that the payment part is a key hash

verification: Verify agent, read-only, 2026-10-22: 3 findings of scope merge-duplicate-tests, to-property or main-bug; 3 confirmed, 0 narrowed, 0 disproved and dropped [P2-12]. Other findings are unverified.
